To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) MLSD is a very powerful technique to overcome turbulence induced signal fading, but is computationally infeasible in most cases; 2) MLSD is feasible with spatial diversity reception, but at the price of a diversity gain penalty due to correlation between the fading in the different receivers; and 3) ML detection with multiple receivers can be used to reduce this penalty, at a cost of additional complexity.

ML detection is a viable option to overcome turbulence induced signal fading, but that it can be very computationally expensive; MLSD can be used to further improve detection performance at the cost of a significant increase in complexity; spatial diversity reception can be used to mitigate turbulence induced fading; ML detection in spatially diverse reception can be used reduce the penalty caused by correlation in the fading at different spatially diverse receivers.

1) the MLSD receiver achieves the best performance, 2) the symbol by symbol ML receiver is the most practical, and 3) spatial diversity can be used to mitigate fading in free space optical communication.
